tasks.task: Mobilise site and establish site controls
tasks.scope: Set up site office, establish resident liaison contact, briefing protocols, erect site signage, confirm waste chute location and timing window (7am–9am Kiora Lane), verify scaffold anchoring points.
hazards: Trip or slip on uneven ground during site setup and signage installation
Manual handling injury — lifting and positioning office containers and materials
Contact with vehicle or delivery traffic during waste chute location confirmation on Kiora Lane
Fall from height — accessing balconies to verify scaffold anchoring points
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — accessing balconies to verify scaffold anchoring points
controls: Obtain signed working at heights permit before accessing any balcony or elevated area to verify scaffold anchoring points.
Brief all personnel on site boundaries, traffic routes, waste chute timing (7am–9am Kiora Lane), and occupied building protocols before work starts.
Install site signage at all public-facing boundaries and entry points — minimum 600mm height, visible from street.
Confirm waste chute location with building management and establish 7am–9am exclusion zone on Kiora Lane before site setup.
Position site office container in designated location with level ground — check stability before occupation.
Assign traffic spotter during waste chute location confirmation on Kiora Lane — spotter must maintain continuous watch and stop all movement if pedestrians or vehicles approach.
Access balconies only via scaffolding or EWP — never use ladders or informal means to verify scaffold anchoring points.
Attach safety harness to certified anchor point before stepping onto any balcony — confirm anchor point capacity with scaffold engineer.
tell building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not access balconies to verify scaffold anchoring points until: working at heights permit is signed and scaffold engineer has certified anchor point locations and load capacity.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or certified anchor point is missing before any elevated access.
🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicles or pedestrians enter Kiora Lane waste chute zone during 7am–9am window — resume only when area is clear.
🛑 STOP WORK if: site office container is not level or shows signs of instability — reposition or replace before occupancy.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Establish resident liaison contact and confirm communication method (phone/email/on-site notice) before mobilisation.
Brief all site personnel on noise-sensitive hours and occupied building protocols — record attendance and sign-off.
Confirm with building management the exact waste chute location, drop point safety, and any timing restrictions beyond 7am–9am window.
Retain scaffold engineer certification of anchoring points — file in site office and verify current before any elevated work.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before starting
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works before commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: Hard hat — mandatory on entire site during setup.
High-visibility vest — mandatory during traffic zone work on Kiora Lane.
Safety harness and lanyard — mandatory for all balcony and elevated access.
Steel-capped boots — mandatory for site setup and material handling.

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.frequency: before each balcony access and daily site start
monitoring.evidence: Signed permit in site office file; harness and anchor point physically confirmed on-site each time.

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.scope: Install scaffold to Suites 7, 8, 11, 12, 14 balconies and terrace via Kiora Lane and courtyard access. Confirm bearing, tie-downs, and fall protection anchor points. Install debris containment netting.
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold failure, collapse, or incomplete guardrailing during erection
Dropped object or tool from height striking person or property below
Contact with overhead obstructions or architectural features during scaffold positioning
Structural failure — bearing, tie-down, or anchor point inadequacy on existing balconies
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — scaffold failure, collapse, or incomplete guardrailing during erection
controls: Obtain engineer certification of bearing capacity and tie-down adequacy for each balcony before erection starts.
Install temporary edge protection or guardrailing on all exposed edges during and after scaffold erection.
Verify scaffold is fully tagged and certified by licensed scaffolder before workers access the structure.
Install debris netting to full height and perimeter to contain dropped objects and tools.
Confirm all tie-downs are secured to engineer-approved anchor points before loading scaffold.
Check access routes via Kiora Lane and courtyard are clear of trip hazards and obstacles.
Establish and maintain 3.5 m exclusion zone below elevated work; barricade and signpost to public areas.
Conduct fall protection anchor point load test to 15 kN minimum before harnesses are attached.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start erection until: engineer certification of bearing and tie-down design is received and verified on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to incomplete scaffold until: fully tagged, guardrailing complete, and debris netting installed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any tie-down or bearing shows visible damage, movement, or settlement during or after installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrailing or fall protection is incomplete or damaged before worker access.
🛑 STOP WORK if: debris netting has holes, gaps, or loose edges that allow dropped objects to fall uncontained.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display Working at Heights Permit signed by competent supervisor before erection starts.
Provide Noise Management Plan to building occupants 48 hours before work; compliance check daily.
Provide Dust Containment Plan; install hoarding or plastic sheeting to separate work from occupied suites.
Brief all workers on scaffold erection sequence, tie-down locations, and exclusion zone boundaries before start.
Record engineer certification, scaffold tag certificate, and load test results on site file; make available for inspection.
ppe: Full-body harness with shock absorber and lanyard (when working at height above 2 m without guardrailing)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify engineer bearing certification and tie-down design before erection; confirm licensed scaffolder tag on structure.
monitoring.frequency: before erection starts; daily visual check during erection; final check before worker access
monitoring.evidence: Engineer letter on file; scaffold tag visible and legible; load test record; photographic record of completed installation

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Hold point: latent condition framework — toxic material investigation
tasks.scope: Before removal works start, confirm lead paint and asbestos survey status. If pre-existing materials suspected or detected during removal, stop work and tell principal. Document and manage as variation if removal required.
hazards: Inhalation of lead dust during disturbance of lead-painted surfaces without survey confirmation
Exposure to asbestos fibres if friable or non-friable asbestos is disturbed without declaration and control
Skin contact with hazardous materials if identity and safe handling method are unknown
Work proceeding without stop-work authority, creating liability cascade for downstream tasks
tasks.dominant_hazard: Exposure to asbestos fibres if friable or non-friable asbestos is disturbed without declaration and control
controls: Obtain and review lead paint survey report before any removal work starts.
If survey reports are absent or inconclusive, stop work immediately and tell principal.
If friable asbestos is identified, prohibit disturbance and engage licensed asbestos removalist.
If non-friable asbestos is identified, map location, establish exclusion zone, and brief all workers on no-disturbance protocol.
If lead paint is identified on surfaces to be disturbed, obtain lead removal method statement from principal before proceeding.
Photograph and document location, type, and condition of all detected hazardous materials on site.
If hazardous materials are discovered during removal work, stop immediately, isolate area, and tell principal and site supervisor.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not disturb any material suspected to contain asbestos until: licensed asbestos removalist confirms safe removal method or material is certified asbestos-free
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: lead paint survey or asbestos survey is absent or inconclusive at task commencement
🛑 STOP WORK if: friable asbestos or suspect friable material is encountered during removal work
🛑 STOP WORK if: unidentified hazardous material or suspected lead dust is generated during disturbance of painted surfaces
admin: Brief all removal workers on location and identity of known hazardous materials on first day.
Record receipt and review of survey reports in site induction log.
Establish material variation claim procedure with principal if asbestos or lead removal is required.
Maintain photographic record of all detected hazardous materials and their location.
tell principal within 24 hours of any variation scope triggered by hazardous material discovery.
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (fit-tested and assigned) if lead dust disturbance is suspected or confirmed
Disposable coveralls (Type 5) if handling confirmed lead-painted materials

monitoring.critical_control: SDS on site, PPE matched to chemical, ventilation confirmed
monitoring.frequency: Before task commencement and daily during removal phase
monitoring.evidence: Survey reports filed on site, induction record signed by workers, photographic record of hazmat locations, stop-work log if triggered

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Hold point: latent condition framework
responsibility.WKR: Perform Hold point: latent condition framework per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing, screed, and tiling
tasks.scope: Strip failed membrane, screed, and tile bed from balconies (Suites 7, 8, 11, 12, 14) and terrace. Remove existing silica-producing materials via containment. Load debris to chute for 7am–9am waste removal window.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust during dry cutting, grinding, or chipping of screed and tile bed
Fall from height — loss of balance on wet or uneven substrate during removal work on elevated balconies
Manual handling injury — lifting and carrying heavy tiles, screed fragments, and waste debris
Cut or laceration — contact with sharp tile edges, fractured tile shards, or cutting tools
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of silica dust during dry cutting, grinding, or chipping of screed and tile bed
controls: Wet all screed and tile surfaces with low-pressure water spray before cutting, grinding, or chipping — keep substrate damp throughout removal.
Connect dust extraction to all power tools (angle grinder, diamond blade saw) — run continuously during cutting; maintain suction during pauses.
Wear respiratory protective equipment (P2 or P3 mask) fitted before starting work — replace mask when resistance increases or after 4 hours.
Erect dust containment barrier (plastic sheeting minimum 1.8 m height) around balcony work area — seal gaps and maintain throughout task.
Remove tile and screed by hand chipping or wet cutting only — prohibit dry grinding or high-velocity impact methods on this substrate.
Barricade all work edges with yellow-and-black tape at minimum 2 m from drop zone — position spotter to monitor falling fragments.
Load all debris into lined waste chute immediately after removal — do not stockpile on elevated surface longer than 30 minutes.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (nitrile-coated or leather) and eye protection— check gloves before each use for tears.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start removal work until: dust containment barrier is erected to full height, sealed at base and gaps, and water supply is confirmed live and adequate pressure.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression equipment fails or water supply stops — do not resume cutting or grinding until system is repaired and suction or spray is restored.
🛑 STOP WORK if: RPE mask resistance is high or worker reports difficulty breathing — replace mask immediately and refit before resuming work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: balcony becomes wet or slippery from spray activity and no anti-slip mat or surface preparation is in place — dry surface or apply grit tape before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed Working at Heights Permit and Dust Containment Plan before 7:00 am start on each removal day.
Confirm water supply pressure via test spray 15 minutes before crew arrival — log pressure reading and time.
Conduct pre-work toolbox talk on silica exposure, wet-work requirement, and RPE fit-test procedure — all workers sign attendance sheet.
Schedule waste chute booking to align with 7:00–9:00 am removal window — confirm collection time with site waste contractor.
Record daily water usage, dust suppression downtime, and mask replacements in site diary.
tell building occupants 48 hours before work — provide noise and dust advisory; confirm access to balconies is clear.
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment: P2 or P3 particulate mask (fit-tested), fresh mask each 4 hours or when resistance high
Hearing protection (earplugs or muffs) if grinding or impact tools used

monitoring.critical_control: follow water spray contact with all cut surfaces — no visible dust plume during grinding or chipping.
monitoring.who: Supervisor on-site + independent worker on adjacent balcony watching fragment fall zone
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during active cutting; check water pressure and dust extraction suction before each tool restart
monitoring.evidence: Damp substrate visual check, dust extraction suction felt at tool inlet, spotter log of no fragments landing outside barrier, daily water pressure reading in site diary

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing waterproofing, screed, and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing waterproofing, screed, and per SWMS

tasks.task: Investigate and repair Suite 7 slab crack
tasks.scope: Open and check crack in Suite 7 slab. Clean and assess structural integrity. Perform concrete repair (filling, epoxy injection, or patching) per engineer direction. Hold substrate until waterproofing contractor confirms readiness.
hazards: Fall from height — loss of balance while working at the crack location on elevated balcony
Dust or fragment inhalation during concrete opening, cleaning, and assessment
Cut or abrasion — contact with exposed reinforcement or rough concrete edges
Chemical exposure — inhalation or skin contact during epoxy injection or concrete repair application
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance while working at the crack location on elevated balcony
controls: Obtain engineer assessment and written repair method before opening crack.
Establish exclusion zone 2 m around work area — barricade and post warning signs.
Wet concrete surfaces with fine spray before opening crack — suppress dust continuously during breaking and cleaning.
Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) during concrete breaking, chiselling, and dust-generating cleaning work.
Use portable dust extractor with HEPA filter attached to breaking tools — capture dust at source.
check exposed reinforcement for sharp edges — file or cap before handling.
Obtain product SDS and confirm compatibility with concrete substrate before epoxy or repair application.
Ventilate work area — open windows or use local exhaust ventilation during chemical application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply epoxy or patch material until: engineer confirms crack cleaning method and repair specification in writing
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not release substrate for waterproofing until: waterproofing contractor inspects repair and confirms slab readiness
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses balance or feels unstable on elevated work platform — move and reassess access method
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression fails or respiratory protection is removed during dust-generating work
🛑 STOP WORK if: epoxy or chemical product spills on skin or in eyes — isolate area and provide first aid immediately
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed working at heights permit before starting elevated work.
Brief all workers on engineer repair specification and approved crack-opening method.
Post site notice advising occupants of dust control and after-hours access restrictions.
Record baseline photos of crack before opening — document repair method and final condition for warranty.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: P2 respirator (fit-tested) — during concrete breaking and dust generation

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.who: Supervisor — continuous observation during breaking and cleaning phases
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during dust generation; check respirator fit before each session
monitoring.evidence: Dust suppression visible on surfaces; worker fit-check card signed; baseline and completion photos on file

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.scope: check all waterproofed areas, tiled finishes, balustrades, and render patches. fix defects, repoint, and touch-up coatings. Confirm resident satisfaction and remedial WHS compliance.
hazards: Fall from height — loss of balance during inspection of elevated balconies and terrace finishes
Contact with wet or tacky surfaces during repointing, touch-up coatings, or grouting
Chemical exposure — inhalation or skin contact with coating or sealant products during application
Cut or abrasion — handling sharp-edged defective tiles or balustrade components during make-good work
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance during inspection of elevated balconies and terrace finishes
controls: Obtain signed working at heights permit before starting any elevated inspection or defect rectification work.
Check balcony and terrace edge protection — handrails, balusters, and infill panels — for damage before each work session.
Use safety harness and lanyard clipped to fixed anchor point when working at leading edges or unprotected perimeters above 2 metres.
Wet all surfaces with water mist before repointing or coating to prevent dust inhalation and improve grip.
Confirm product SDS on site and brief all workers on hazards — inhalation risk, skin contact, ventilation requirements — before opening containers.
Wear respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) when sanding, grinding, or dry-brushing render patches or tile defects.
Cordon off work area with barrier tape and signage to prevent residents and bystanders entering wet or newly coated zones.
Stop work immediately if any balustrade component shows movement, cracking, or loose fixings — do not proceed until certified repair complete.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start elevated defect rectification until: working at heights permit is signed and displayed on site, and harness attachment points are verified safe by supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply coating or sealant products until: product SDS is on site, workers have received hazard briefing, and ventilation or RPE availability is confirmed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any balustrade, balcony edge, or elevated work surface shows structural movement, crack propagation, or loose fixings during inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions (wind >30 km/h, rain, low visibility) make safe harness use or surface grip impossible.
🛑 STOP WORK if: resident or unauthorised person attempts access to cordoned work area or wet surface zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain working at heights permit — signed before each elevated task.
Obtain noise management plan — tell residents of work timing where defect rectification uses power tools.
Obtain dust containment plan — plastic sheeting or hoarding around balcony or terrace work zone before starting.
Verify workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Obtain product SDS for all coatings, sealants, membranes, and grout products — store on site and accessible.
Brief residents on work scope, timing, and access restrictions before work starts each day.
Record defect inspection findings (photos, locations, repair method) and post-repair resident sign-off confirming satisfaction.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (class 2 fall arrest) — clipped to fixed anchor when working at leading edges or above 2 metres.
Hard hat — worn always on elevated work platforms or balconies.
eye protection— impact-resistant, worn during tile removal, cutting, or dry-surface work.
Respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum when grinding, sanding, or creating dust during render or tile defect work.
Non-slip footwear — worn on all wet or newly coated surfaces.
High-visibility vest — worn on occupied sites to alert residents and other trades.

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each work shift and before each elevated task within shift
monitoring.evidence: Signed permit on site; visual confirmation of harness attachment; photo of anchor point and rigging

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: check per specification, photograph defects, report issues

tasks.task: Prepare substrate and apply waterproofing membrane
tasks.scope: Clean and prime substrate on balconies (Suites 7, 8, 11, 12, 14) and terrace. Apply waterproofing membrane per specification. check seams and penetrations. Allow cure time per product data.
hazards: Fall from height — slippery substrate or loss of balance during cleaning and priming operations on elevated balconies
Chemical exposure — inhalation or skin contact with primer, membrane, or solvent vapours
Contact dermatitis or chemical burn from waterproofing products
Slip or trip on wet cleaned or primed surfaces during application and inspection
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — slippery substrate or loss of balance during cleaning and priming operations on elevated balconies
controls: Obtain SDS for primer and membrane product before work starts; brief all workers on hazard summary, first aid, and ventilation requirements.
Establish continuous cross-flow or local exhaust ventilation at application and curing areas to remove solvent or primer vapours; check air movement with smoke test before starting.
Clean substrate with damp cloth or pressure wash at low pressure (<80 bar) to avoid dust generation; allow complete dryness before priming.
Apply primer per product data sheet; use only in natural ventilation or with respiratory protection if vapour concentration cannot be monitored.
Barricade wet primed or membrane surfaces with high-visibility tape and warning signs; prohibit pedestrian access until surface is dry and grip is restored.
check all seams, penetrations, and edges for complete membrane coverage and adhesion; document non-conformance and fix before cure time starts.
Confirm membrane has fully cured per product SDS (minimum time stated on container label) before allowing foot traffic or load placement.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves during cleaning, priming, and membrane application; remove and dispose of gloves immediately after use.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer or membrane until: substrate is clean, dry, and SDS has been reviewed with all workers on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or final inspection until: membrane has cured per product SDS minimum time and surface grip is verified.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails or vapour odour becomes strong; evacuate area and re-establish air movement before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker shows signs of chemical exposure (dizziness, headache, shortness of breath); remove worker from area immediately and seek medical advice.
🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or lanyard shows visible damage, fraying, or detachment; do not re-use until repaired or replaced by certified technician.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display working at heights permit signed by site supervisor before starting elevated work on any suite or terrace.
Obtain SDS for all primers, membranes, and solvents on site; keep in toolbox or site office and make available to all workers.
Confirm waterproofer holds current AS 3740 competency or equivalent licensed credential before application starts.
Record SDS review and ventilation system test in site diary before any application begins.
Document final membrane inspection: date, suite number, seam condition, penetration coverage, and any defects found; retain with project records.
Record cure time start and completion date on site plan; do not mark suite as 'ready for final testing' until cure time has elapsed.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
tell affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator (fit-tested, sealed before use)

monitoring.critical_control: Check ventilation air movement with smoke test every shift before priming or membrane application.
monitoring.frequency: before each application session / continuous during work
monitoring.evidence: Smoke test result recorded in site diary; visible air movement at application area; no strong solvent odour detectable at 1 metre distance

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Prepare substrate and apply waterproofing
responsibility.WKR: Perform Prepare substrate and apply waterproofing per SWMS

tasks.task: Install tiles, render patches, and balustrades
tasks.scope: Lay new tiles on balconies, terrace, and Suite 7 awning. Patch and finish render on facade elements. Install replacement glass balustrades to engineer specification. Apply rust treatment to exposed steel elements.
hazards: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip on wet adhesive or grout during tile laying on elevated balconies and terrace
Cut or laceration — contact with sharp tile edges or glass balustrade edges during handling and installation
Manual handling injury — lifting and positioning heavy tiles, balustrade panels, and equipment
Eye injury — splinter or dust particle during balustrade installation or rust treatment application
Chemical exposure — inhalation or skin contact with rust treatment products or grout additives
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip on wet adhesive or grout during tile laying on elevated balconies and terrace
controls: Confirm working at heights permit signed and dated before starting any elevated tile work on balconies, terrace, or awning.
Lay fall arrest anchor points and certified harnesses on balcony and terrace edges before tile laying starts.
Apply waterproof membrane to all substrate surfaces per AS 3740 before laying tiles.
Mix tile adhesive and grout to correct consistency — test adhesive grab strength on scrap tile before laying production tiles.
Lay tiles in sequence that maintains dry work platform — isolate wet adhesive areas with wet floor signs and barriers.
Wear anti-slip footwear on all wet tile and grout areas — change footwear if grip reduces.
Handle all tiles and glass balustrade panels with cut-resistant gloves — check hands for cuts after each handling session.
Install glass balustrades to engineer specification drawing — stop work if panels do not match drawing dimensions or bearing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lay tiles until: waterproof membrane cured per product SDS and substrate is dry to touch
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install glass balustrades until: engineer certification received and all dimension checks passed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker loses balance on wet tile or adhesive surface or falls to harness — review cause before resuming
🛑 STOP WORK if: rust treatment sprayed in wind speeds below 2 m/s or when occupants present downwind of application
🛑 STOP WORK if: glass balustrade panel edges or tile edges cause hand or finger cuts — assess glove adequacy and tool design
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed working at heights permit before each day of elevated tile or balustrade work.
Provide site copy of product SDS for tile adhesive, grout, waterproof membrane, and rust treatment — keep visible at work station.
Verify workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) before task start.
Brief all workers on waterproof membrane curing time, adhesive pot life, and grout additives before mixing.
Record daily fall arrest harness and anchor point check — sign and date before harness use.
tell building occupants of dust containment measures and hoarding location — post contact details for noise or dust complaints.
Conduct noise level check before starting tile cutting or grinding — apply noise management plan if work exceeds 85 dB(A).
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) with organic vapour cartridge for rust treatment spraying
eye protection, glass balustrade fitting, and rust treatment application

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before each work shift at height — daily
monitoring.evidence: Signed and dated harness and anchor point check sheet — photographic record of secure attachment points

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install tiles, render patches, and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install tiles, render patches, and per SWMS

tasks.scope: Remove and replace worn ground-floor tiles with slip-resistant finish. Includes screed and bed preparation. Coordinate with foyer traffic and resident access.
hazards: Slip or trip on wet ground-floor surfaces during removal, substrate preparation, and tile laying
Manual handling injury — lifting and carrying tiles and screed materials
Dust inhalation during screed and tile removal and surface preparation
Contact with foot traffic or resident movement during foyer work coordination
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip or trip on wet ground-floor surfaces during removal, substrate preparation, and tile laying
controls: Wet-mop all work areas and traffic routes every 2 hours during removal and preparation work.
Lay anti-slip matting or absorbent matting on all pedestrian routes in and out of foyer work zone.
Barricade the tile work zone with high-visibility cordon tape — keep residents and traffic 2 m clear.
Remove tiles using wet-cutting method with suppression mist — no dry grinding or hammering.
Vacuum all dust from screed prep using HEPA-filtered extraction before laying new tiles.
Check tile substrate for moisture using probe meter — confirm below 5% before membrane application.
Apply waterproof membrane per product SDS and AS 3740 — verify coverage and cure time before tiling.
Lay tiles with proper bed depth and grouting — check for voids using screed-light method.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply waterproof membrane until: substrate moisture probe reads below 5% and SDS reviewed by applicator
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reopen foyer to traffic until: grout has cured per product SDS and slip-resistance finish is dry
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet tile removal or screed prep creates pooled water or slippery residue not immediately mop-dried
🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA extraction fails or dust visible during screed preparation — repair or replace filter
🛑 STOP WORK if: residents or unauthorised persons enter the barricaded work zone
admin: Brief all workers and residents on wet-floor hazard and foyer access restrictions before work starts.
Establish a daily checklist: moisture meter calibration, matting condition, barricade integrity, HEPA filter status.
Post wet-floor warning signs at all foyer entry points — rotate every shift.
Coordinate with building manager for resident notification of access restrictions and noise/dust windows.
Keep product SDS and AS 3740 waterproofing checklist on site — sign off membrane application before tiling.
Record substrate moisture readings and cure times daily — evidence for defect liability.
ppe: Safety shoes with slip-resistant sole — mandatory on all staff in foyer zone
Dust mask or P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) — during tile removal and screed preparation (if HEPA extraction unavailable)
Eye protection (eye protection— tile cutting and membrane application

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift start, every 2 hours during removal/prep, after any wet process
monitoring.evidence: Daily wet-floor log with time stamps, moisture meter readings logged, photographic record of matting condition and barricade integrity

responsibility.WKR: Perform Replace ground-floor slippery tiles per SWMS

tasks.scope: Reinstall awning frame, glazing, and fixings. Reinstall door seals, downpipes, and drainage outlets. Test water runoff and confirm proper fall and clearance.
hazards: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip during awning frame installation on elevated balcony
Dropped object — glazing, fixings, or frame components striking person or property below
Cut or laceration — contact with sharp metal frame edges or glass glazing during handling
Misalignment or structural failure — incorrect reinstallation of awning frame or drainage outlets
Manual handling injury — lifting and positioning heavy awning and glazing components
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — loss of balance or slip during awning frame installation on elevated balcony
controls: Confirm awning frame alignment with engineer-approved drawings before lifting into position
Establish exclusion zone 6 metres below awning work area — barricade and post lookout
Install edge protection netting or rigid screens on balcony perimeter — prevent dropped glazing or fixings
